assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Bronze
items.clue: An alloy of copper and tin, used for statues, ornaments and bells.

items.label: Brass
items.clue: An alloy of copper and zinc, used for musical instruments, door fittings and taps.

items.label: Cross-links
items.clue: Strong bonds joining one polymer chain to another, which stop the chains moving past each other on heating.

items.label: Matrix (binder)
items.clue: The material in a composite that surrounds and holds the reinforcement, for example the cement in concrete.

questions.stem: Soda-lime glass is made by heating a mixture of which substances?

options.text: Sand with boron trioxide, heated strongly
Sand on its own, melted in a hot furnace
Sand, sodium carbonate and limestone
Clay, limestone and sodium chloride

questions.explanation: Most of the glass we use is soda-lime glass, made by heating a mixture of sand, sodium carbonate and limestone.

questions.stem: How does borosilicate glass differ from soda-lime glass?

options.text: It melts at a much lower temperature
It is made from pure sand and nothing else
It melts easily once it gets hot enough
It melts at a higher temperature

questions.explanation: Borosilicate glass, made from sand and boron trioxide, melts at higher temperatures than soda-lime glass.

questions.stem: How are clay ceramics such as bricks and pottery made?

options.text: Wet clay is shaped and then heated in a furnace
Clay is melted and poured into a cold mould
Dry clay powder is pressed and left to set
Clay is mixed with sand and melted down

questions.explanation: Clay ceramics, including pottery and bricks, are made by shaping wet clay and then heating in a furnace.

questions.stem: LD and HD poly(ethene) are both produced from ethene. Why do they have different properties?

options.text: They are built from two different monomers
A different catalyst and conditions are used
HD poly(ethene) is pressed hard after it is made
The HD chains contain a second element

questions.explanation: The properties of polymers depend on the monomer and on the conditions under which they are made, so the same ethene gives two different materials.

questions.stem: Why do thermosoftening polymers melt when they are heated?

options.text: The strong covalent bonds along the chains break
Any solid will melt if it is heated enough
Separate chains are held only by weak forces
The polymer is a liquid that was frozen

questions.explanation: The chains are separate and tangled, with only weak forces between them, so they slide apart when heated.

questions.stem: Why do thermosetting polymers keep their shape when they are heated?

options.text: They only melt above about a thousand degrees
The covalent bonds in the chains never break
They contain no carbon that could be melted
Cross-links join the chains to each other

questions.explanation: The chains in a thermosetting polymer are joined by cross-links, so they cannot slide apart and the polymer does not melt.

questions.stem: Most composites are made of two materials. How are those two materials arranged?

options.text: A matrix surrounds and binds together fibres or fragments
Two materials are melted into a single new substance
Fibres surround the matrix and hold it firmly in place
Two elements are joined chemically to give a compound

questions.explanation: Most composites are made of a matrix or binder surrounding and binding together fibres or fragments of the reinforcement.

questions.stem: Which of these materials is a composite?

options.text: Brass, which is copper mixed with zinc
Concrete, gravel held together by cement
Poly(ethene), made from many ethene units
Soda-lime glass, made by melting sand

questions.explanation: Concrete is a composite: cement is the matrix and the gravel is the reinforcement.

questions.stem: A table gives: aluminium alloy, density 2.7 g/cm3, does not shatter; soda-lime glass, density 2.5 g/cm3, shatters when dropped; carbon fibre composite, density 1.6 g/cm3, does not shatter. Which material is lightest for a given volume and survives being dropped?

options.text: Soda-lime glass, since glass is the lightest here
Aluminium alloy, since a metal can never break
The carbon fibre composite, the least dense
Aluminium alloy, as it is the densest one

questions.stem: A saucepan handle must not soften on the hot hob and must not conduct heat well. Which material is most suitable?

options.text: A polymer with strong covalent chains
A toughened soda-lime glass
A hard-wearing steel alloy
A thermosetting polymer

questions.explanation: Thermosetting polymers do not melt when heated and, being polymers, are poor conductors of heat.
